name: Grant Easel
preparty_markdown:
Grant is the person wealthy collectors call when they want something no one else seems able to find.

Charming, fast-talking, and always perfectly dressed, he insists that art dealing is mostly about trust,

discretion, and knowing which flight lands in Geneva before breakfast. He has brokered several loans in

tonight's exhibition and knows half the room professionally.

HOW TO PLAY THEM

Smooth, sociable, opportunistic, impossible to embarrass. Treat every conversation like a deal that has not yet revealed

itself.

WHAT YOU ALREADY KNOW

• Has represented Theo Glass in private acquisitions, though neither likes admitting how often they need the other.

• Competes with Conrad Gavel for major consignments.

• Daphne Palette considers him useful but never entirely trustworthy.

COSTUME

Fashion-forward dinner jacket or sharp suit, polished shoes, expensive-looking watch (real or fake), pocket square. Optional

slim catalogue with sticky tabs.

OPTIONAL QUIPS

“Provenance is just biography with invoices.”

“I never pressure anyone. I simply describe the consequences of waiting.”

Do not invent private history with Sterling Voss before game night. Your sealed party-night packet will reveal what your character actually knows

about him.

name: Margot Ledger
role: Chief Financial Officer of the Meridian Museum
preparty_markdown:
Margot can tell you exactly how much tonight's floral installation cost, which donor paid for it, and which line

item everyone is pretending it came from. She is sharp, stylish, practical, and chronically surrounded by

people with expensive visions and no budgets. If the museum survives its ambitions, Margot will probably be

the reason.

HOW TO PLAY THEM

Quick, pragmatic, wry, unimpressed by grandeur for grandeur's sake. You notice costs other people pretend not to see.

WHAT YOU ALREADY KNOW

• Works constantly with Adrian Vellum and Helena Cross.

• Has a friendly rivalry with Riley Bloom, whose gala ideas tend to arrive before their price tags.

• Beatrice Plinth likes Margot because she asks questions trustees hate answering.

COSTUME

Modern cocktail attire or tailored suit; sleek, practical, expensive-looking without being flashy. Carry a small ledger,

calculator, or pen clipped to a folder.

OPTIONAL QUIPS

“Every priceless object has an insurance value. I checked.”

“Beauty is subjective. The invoice is not.”

Do not invent private history with Sterling Voss before game night. Your sealed party-night packet will reveal what your character actually knows

about him.
